text.en: Prakash visits his cousin Ravi and learns about Lagori, a game of seven flat stones, called Satoliya in his home state of Rajasthan. The next day the Sundarpur Tigers play the Green Warriors and win. In this chapter you will read the play, learn about traditional games, rearrange words into sentences, tell a sentence from a question and build a team badge.

Ravi and his cousin Prakash go to the children's park, where friends are talking about tomorrow's Lagori match. The friends want Prakash in the team because he is a quick runner. Prakash has never heard of Lagori, so everyone looks at him in surprise, and Nidhi explains that it is a game of seven stones. Imran, a champion of the game, explains how it is played.
Seven flat stones are stacked one above the other in the centre of the field. One team knocks down the stones with a ball, and then the same team tries to rebuild the stack. The other team throws the ball at the builders to stop them. The field has a boundary line and players must not go beyond it. Prakash says that in Rajasthan the same game is called Satoliya, so one game can have different names in different places.
The next day the referee blew the whistle and Deepa took the first shot, scattering the stones and making everyone cheer. The Sundarpur Tigers began to rebuild the stack while the Green Warriors threw the ball at them. Ravi ducked and Deepa dodged just in time. Nidhi placed the fourth and fifth stones and Ravi placed the sixth, and Prakash set the seventh stone on top just before the final whistle. The referee announced that the Sundarpur Tigers had won.
Both teams shook hands and appreciated each other, and the villagers cheered for both teams. The referee lifted the hands of both captains because a good game is about teamwork and fair play, not only winning. Deepa said it was even better than video games, and Ravi said they should play traditional games more.
A match is a game played between teams. Stacked means piled one above the other. An opponent is a person or team you play against. A boundary is a line that marks the edge. A referee is the person who controls the game. Dodged means moved quickly to avoid something. Teamwork is working together. Warriors are brave fighters. A cousin is the child of your uncle or aunt.
A sentence is a group of words that makes complete sense. It starts with a capital letter and usually ends with a full stop. Rearrange the words: The field is marked with a boundary. Everybody looked at Prakash with surprise. I saw a peacock dancing in the rain. A question asks something. It starts with a capital letter and ends with a question mark. What is your name? and Where do you stay? are questions. My name is Sonam is a sentence that tells something.
Make a team badge with a name like Rainbow Runners and symbols like stacked stones, a ball or joined hands, and explain what it means. Talk about a community game played in your colony or village and whether you took part. Ask people at home about traditional games and learn one.
Let us think about the story. Lagori is a game in which players try to break a pile of flat stones with a ball and rebuild the pile before being hit. Think and discuss: the villagers clapped for both teams and the referee lifted both captains’ hands because good sportsmanship matters more than winning. Teamwork helps in games because each player has a job, and the team wins when everyone plays together. Some say a game like Lagori is more exciting than video games because we run, laugh and play with friends. What do you think, and why?

problem.en: Make a sentence: boundary / field / is / the / marked / a / with.

text.en: Look for the subject.

why.en: The field is what we talk about.

text.en: Say what is done to it: is marked with a boundary.

why.en: Put the words in a sensible order.

text.en: So: The field is marked with a boundary.

why.en: Start with a capital letter and end with a full stop.

problem.en: Is this a sentence or a question: Where do you stay?

text.en: Does it ask something?
It ends with a question mark.
So it is a question.

why.en: My name is Sonam is a sentence.

prompt.en: Tell the story of the Lagori match and say why both captains were cheered.

points.en: Lagori is a game of seven flat stones, also called Satoliya.
The Sundarpur Tigers beat the Green Warriors.
Prakash set the seventh stone on top.
Both teams were cheered for fair play.
A sentence tells something; a question asks something.
